5. The opposite party-respondent further submits that the trial of the. Special Case No.08 of was conducted by the Divisional Special Judge, Khulna under the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and after completion of the trial the Divisional Special Judge, Khulna acquitted the opposite party respondent from the charge brought against him under section 477(Ka)/409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1947. 

 10. That it is stated that the trial of the Special Case No.08 of 2007 was conducted by the Divisional Special Judge Khulna under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and after completion of the trial the learned Divisional Special Judge Khulna acquitted the Opposite Party/Respondent from the charge brought against him under section 477(Ka)/409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1947. 

 That it is stated that the instant :appeal is not maintainable and without jurisdiction as the appeal was filed by the Deputy Commissioner of Khulna on behalf of Government under section 417 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 That it is stated that section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 deals with the procedure in respect of appeal against the judgment and order passed by Special Judge in a proceeding conducted under the said Act and according to Section 10(2) of the said Act, only Anti-Corruption Commission is authorized to direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal against the order of acquittal passed by the Special Judge. 

 That it is stated that in the instant appeal there is no reference that the Anti-Corruption Commission ever directed the Deputy Commissioner of Khulna or the Government-or the Public Prosecutor or the Attorney General Office to file the instant appeal. Rather it is evident from paragraph 2 of the Condonation of delay Application that, on 25-07-2011 the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna referred the impugned judgment and other along with necessary papers to the Solicitor Office of the Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs with a request to prefer an appeal. Thereafter on 16-08-2011 the Solicitor Office of the Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs instructed the Attorney General Office to prefer the instant appeal against the impugned judgment and order. Accordingly the Attorney General office filed the instant appeal with an application for condonation of delay of 167 days. 

 11. That it is evident from the application for condonation of delay that the Deputy Commissioner of Khulna or the Solicitor Office or the Attorney General Office never took permission from the Anti-Corruption Commission to prefer the instant appeal and the Anti-Corruption Commission also did not direct the Attorney General Office or the Government under section 10(2) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 to prefer the instant appeal and as such the instant appeal is without jurisdiction and not maintainable and therefore the application for condonation of delay is liable to be rejected with cost. 

 12. That the learned Advocate for the opposite Party submits further that the impugned judgment and order was passed by a Special Judge appointed under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and permission from the Anti-Corruption Commission to prefer any appeal against the Judgment and order of acquittal passed by a Special Judge is condition precedent and in the instant appeal there is no such permission and as such the application for condonation of delay should be rejected with cost. 

 13. The petitioner is a poor government servant and due to the impugned case he has been suspended from his job for last 12 years and for the last 12 years he did not get his salary and service benefit due to the said false case. After delivery of the impugned judgment of acquittal various occasions including 1.0-10-2010, and 17-04-2010 the opposite party/ Respondent applied to the Mongla Port Authority to allow him to join his post, however the authority without any valid reason and with a malafide intention restrained the Opposite party to join his post and also denied to give his arrear salary and service benefit. 

 15. We also found that the appellant in order to condone the delay in filing the Criminal Appeal must explain each day's delay and explanation of delay in lump is not at all permissible under section 5 of the Limitation Act. Here in the instant application for condonation of delay the appellant/petitioner failed to explain each day's delay in filing the appeal. The Act and conduct of the appellant in filing the instant appeal seems to us is intentional and deliberate negligence and latches on the part of the appellant. The appellant/petitioner was not at all vigilant and sincere to file the instant appeal in time which amounts to deliberate negligence on the part of the appellant. Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not provide any Special concession to the government in respect of limitation in filing the appeal. 

 In respect of delay the Private Party and the Government stand on the same footing but from the perusal of the application for condonation of delay, we find the delay of 167 days as caused in filing the instant Criminal appeal by the appellant government is intentional and deliberate negligence and latches on the part of the appellant. In such situation no special consideration has been provided in section 5 of the Limitation Act in respect of filing appeal by the Government. In this respect the Appellant ought to have explain the each day's delay in prosecuting-the instant appeal very meticulously but on perusal of the explanation and the reasons for delay as given in the application for condonation of delay we find that the very conduct of the appellant is very much negligent and not at all sincere and serious. The explanation as given in paragraph 2 and 3 of the application for condonation of delay are not at all sufficient for condoning the delay of 167 days in filing the Criminal Appeal and the delay as caused in filing the appeal is not at all unintentional but intentional. The learned Advocate for the opposite party respondent in course of his submissions referred section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and also referred the case of the State represented by Solicitor to the Government of Blangladesh Vs Wanur Rahman and others reported in 40 DLR Page 346.
